sar.narrative: Suspicious Activity Report for CASE-014 documents a coordinated fraud ring operating through a shared iOS device fingerprint. The investigation was initiated when transaction 4012211 received a real-time risk score of 0.83, amounting to $1,152.70 [EV-28b3c385]. The originating card SC-03014-K956 exhibited anomalous velocity with four online transactions in 48 hours, far exceeding its $290.54 historical average [EV-74fd18a5, EV-1e019e4c]. Device linkage analysis identified 17 additional cards sharing the identical device profile, encompassing all ten connected cards in this case [EV-d09d544c]. Within that device cluster, four cards carried confirmed fraud verdicts, establishing an 18-card fraud ring [EV-08118e6b]. The customer reported no authorization for the disputed transactions and retained physical possession of their card [EV-9e53efe9]. Total exposure across four transactions reaches $1,162.14 with an assessed fraud probability of 82.4%. The fraud pattern is classified as undocumented, with one similar prior case CC-4327 referenced for pattern continuity. No legitimate travel or purchase explanation was identified for the current activity, contrasting with one previously cleared case for this customer [EV-4beb6489]. The evidence supports a finding of organized card-not-present fraud facilitated by device compromise or credential sharing across the ring.
